title: Opportunistic burst fencing and backfill PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an opportunistic burst and backfill subsystem for Dedicated capacity to allow tenants to safely consume spare GPU headroom while guaranteeing isolation and predictable preemption behavior. This PRD defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, telemetry, and operational controls for fencing opportunistic workloads and backfilling unused capacity without degrading reserved-tenancy SLOs.
background: Customers on Dedicated pools desire lower unit cost by using spare capacity for short bursts. Current approaches either aggressively preempt or risk interfering with reserved tenants. Previous PRDs covered reserve windows, soft-evict, and fairshare; this document focuses on an opportunistic layer that is explicitly fenced, billed differently, and provides explicit backfill guarantees and graceful preemption semantics.
goals: Enable safe use of spare GPU capacity by opportunistic workloads without impacting reserved tenant latency SLOs
Provide transparent preemption semantics and telemetry for both opportunistic and reserved tenants
Offer controls to operators and customers to opt-in/out, set backfill budgets, and configure fencing sensitivity
Ensure billing and quota reporting separates opportunistic usage from reserved consumption
non_goals: Building a full spot-market auction or secondary tenant marketplace in this phase
Changing model-level runtime semantics (e.g., KV cache sharing) beyond isolation boundaries
scope: Phase 1: runtime fencing primitives, backfill allocator that honors preemption latency budgets, console toggles, telemetry and billing flags. Phase 2: customer self-service budgeting, cross-region opportunistic routing, policy templates.
requirements: Runtime must expose an 'opportunistic' placement class that only schedules workloads on nodes with <X% baseline utilisation
Opportunistic tasks must be tagged and visible in telemetry and billing as separate usage streams
Preemption latency target for vacating opportunistic workloads is configurable with default 5s graceful window and hard 30s eviction
Fencing layer must prevent shared-KV/host-level soft locks from promoting interference to reserved tenants
Console controls: per-tenant backfill budget (tokens/hour) and global cluster opportunistic toggle
Operator safety guardrails: automatic drain if reserved-pool p95 latency increases >5% over baseline
Backfill allocator must prefer shortest-running tasks and tasks with preemptible checkpoint hooks
Audit logs for every preemption decision include cause, affected workload, and fallback action
acceptance_criteria: Opportunistic workloads can be enabled on a Dedicated pool via console toggle and API flag
During controlled tests, enabling opportunistic backfill does not increase reserved-tenancy p95 generation latency by more than 5% (measured over 1h window)
Preemption events complete within configured graceful window 95% of the time in test harness
All opportunistic consumption is attributed to a distinct billing code in invoices and in per-tenant cost breakdowns
Operators can set and validate backfill budgets and see real-time consumption metrics in the Console
No data or KV cache leakage occurs between opportunistic and reserved executions in unit and integration tests
Rollout runbooks validated: canary enablement, automatic rollback on threshold breach, and postmortem template completed
success_metrics: Percent of spare capacity utilized by opportunistic workloads (target 30% within 30 days)
Preemption latency P95 for opportunistic tasks (target < 30s)
Reserved-tenant generation latency degradation while opportunistic enabled (target < 5% p95 change)
Customer adoption: number of Dedicated customers opting into opportunistic within 60 days
Billing clarity: percentage of customers who confirm opportunistic line-item billing accuracy (target 95%)
telemetry_and_alerts: Alert: reserved_p95_delta > 5% sustained for 10m => auto-disable opportunistic and page SRE
Audit trail: preemption_decision.log with fields [timestamp, node, tenant, reason, grace_ms]
Console graph: backfill budget burn rate and projected exhaustion ETA
rollout_plan: Developer preview on internal Dedicated cluster (canary) with 1 non-sensitive tenant - weeks 1-2
SRE stress tests with synthetic reserved load while enabling opportunistic at 10/30/50% caps - week 3
Gradual customer opt-in for beta customers with close monitoring and manual safety gates - weeks 4-6
GA behind feature flag with automatic rollback triggers and operator CLI to drain opportunistic workloads - week 8
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Opportunistic workloads cause subtle tail-latency regressions; Mitigation: conservative default caps, operator auto-disable thresholds, expanded telemetry
Risk: Billing attribution errors; Mitigation: separate tagging at scheduler and billing pipeline unit tests before rollout
Risk: Customers misuse opportunistic budgets and see unexpected preemptions; Mitigation: clear UX, warnings in Console, and simulation mode
Risk: Preemption causes downstream errors for long-running stateful jobs; Mitigation: require opt-in labels and recommend checkpoint hooks
dependencies: ENG-25512 (console budget controls and cost breakdowns)
ENG-26003 (audit logging pipeline and billing integration)
